tagline: Between stone fences on the old road to Frankfort.
intro: This stretch of KY 1681 was part of the original road between Frankfort and Lexington, and it is still two lanes all the way, running east from Duckers Station Road in Woodford County to Wolf Run Creek at the edge of Lexington. Underneath lies phosphate-rich limestone, full of springs that flow for miles and then sink out of sight.

For about two miles the trees close overhead and dry-laid limestone fences hold the shoulders. Along the rest of the way come railroad stations, country churches, a tavern from the late eighteenth century and double-fenced fields of Thoroughbreds. There is one four-way stop, at Midway Road.

moments.title: Woodburn Stud
moments.text: The farm where the stallion Lexington stood as America's leading sire for sixteen years was turned over to cattle in the early 1900s, and has bred horses again since 1972 as Airdrie Stud.

moments.title: Old Frankfort Pike Visitor Viewing Area
moments.text: At the roundabout with Alexandria Drive a brick loop trail passes panels on the history of the pike, and a statue of Secretariat keeps the middle of the roundabout.

moments.title: McConnell Springs
moments.text: William McConnell's party camped at these springs in June 1775 and named the camp Lexington, beside water that rises, sinks underground and surfaces again a third of a mile away.
